questions.q: How does a lazy input look to check_lazy_status before it has run?
options: It is the wire as a list
It is left out and raises KeyError
questions.why: A lazy wire with no result yet is marked missing, and arrives as None.

questions.q: A switch uses one lazy branch. How many times is check_lazy_status called?
options: Never, when the switch is on
questions.why: Once to ask, and again after the branch has run. A real run showed check, branch, check, execute.

questions.q: Your check returns ["a"], but a is an optional input with no wire. What happens?
options: a is treated as None and the node runs
The prompt fails: the node says it needs input a, but there is no input
questions.answer: The prompt fails: the node says it needs input a, but there is no input
questions.why: make_input_strong_link raises this while the prompt runs. Validation doesn't call your check.

questions.q: A required input is marked lazy and left unwired. What happens?
questions.why: Lazy says when to evaluate a wire. It doesn't make the input optional.

questions.q: Which is the better way to skip part of a graph?
options: A lazy input, since it never starts the work
questions.answer: A lazy input, since it never starts the work
questions.why: The ExecutionBlocker docstring and the docs both recommend lazy where it can do the job.
